content.short: Aleph Cloud is the AWS of Web3, enabling secure access to off-chain data.
content.description: Aleph Cloud is a decentralized file storage protocol that supports major blockchains, including Solana, Cosmos, Ethereum, and Polygon, enabling a broad range of decentralized applications to reference and retrieve data securely. With just a few lines of code, Aleph Cloud lets developers securely access off-chain data sources while maintaining strict data ownership and user control. Because the storage layer is anchored to the blockchain, the data cannot be tampered with and users retain ownership across the networks it supports.

resources.title: Cloud Sovereignty Should Include Architecture
resources.tldr: Europe's sovereignty debate skips the layer that decides who can switch a system off, who can read what is inside it, and whether anyone outside the provider can verify either answer.

resources.title: Decentralized Cloud Gaming: How It Works
resources.tldr: Games are the hardest test of decentralised compute because latency is unforgiving. Covers distributed GPU rendering and where the model genuinely stops working.

resources.title: Unlocking Confidential Decentralized Computation with GPUs
resources.tldr: Confidential computing on CPUs is well trodden; doing it on GPUs is considerably less so. On what accelerated confidential workloads require and what they still leak.
